original_test_intent: Stress the designated GB-NV-PVP PCIe path with exactly 10,000 approved hot-reset/SBR training transactions and prove that each transaction returns the endpoint to the required link state without new PCIe, GPU, or host errors.
original_method: Resolve the intended Hot Reset versus Secondary Bus Reset semantics and mapped hierarchy; freeze tool/configuration and expected gen/width; capture link/error baseline; execute a ledgered sequence up to 10,000 with per-cycle reset issuance, LTSSM/retrain, enumeration, link, and error outcome; stop on the first unacceptable result; preserve failure chronology and verify controlled recovery.
manual_activity: Owner/FAE approves which bridge/endpoint is reset and the 10,000-cycle envelope; an operator isolates the SUT, monitors console/power/thermal health, and owns recovery from endpoint or host loss.
required_inputs: Authoritative reset mechanism and exact root-port/bridge/endpoint hierarchy
Expected PCIe generation, width, retrain and enumeration deadlines
Cycle definition, cadence, storage/checkpoint integrity, and count rules
Permitted error deltas plus GPU/host/thermal/power aborts
Out-of-band console, state reconciliation, and recovery plan
safety_requirements: Dedicated non-production SUT and explicit 10,000-cycle approval
Verify no unsaved workload and preserve baselines
Bound reset target to the approved hierarchy
Stop on first failed/late retrain, downtrain, enumeration loss, new AER, GPU/host reset, thermal/power fault, or logging gap
Prevent reset continuation after control-channel loss
Never silently retry or clear evidence
agent_execution_scope: Validate configuration, target, baseline, and cycle ledger
Run the approved loop only under active safeguards
Check monotonic cycle IDs and lossless artifacts
Correlate every outcome with link/error/platform health
Do not infer reset semantics, widen target, resume after first fault, replay a failed cycle, or issue the DUT verdict
engineer_actions: Approve reset type, target hierarchy, link acceptance, and 10,000-cycle risk
Define first-fault conditions and missing-evidence policy
Own console recovery and post-failure disposition
Review the ledger and decide PASS, FAIL, or BLOCKED

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: It describes the intended proprietary loop but supplies neither the exact reset command nor sufficient cycle-level evidence, target controls, or stop logic for a 10,000-reset operation.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Use only the approved LTSSM/NVQual reset recipe with an atomic monotonic cycle ledger and hard interlocks that prevent the next reset after any acceptance or collection failure.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: Hot Reset/SBR with training, exactly 10,000 cycles, expected width/speed, no errors, no bundle, and 60/2880-minute allocation remain.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Treat each reset as a transaction that must durably record issuance, topology state, retrain deadline, enumeration, gen/width, error deltas, and health before the next cycle is eligible.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Makes ambiguous reset semantics, evidence durability, first-fault handling, and recovery explicit for the very large cycle count.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: A successful final link state cannot reveal failed intermediate retrains, transient downtraining, missing endpoints, errors, or tool restarts that invalidate the requested sequence.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: A wrong reset scope or uncontrolled loop can repeatedly disrupt multiple endpoints or the host, exhaust logs/storage, strand the GPU, and extend outage or damage investigation.

project_override_considerations: Do not count tool startup, recovery attempts, or automatically repeated cycles toward 10,000. If checkpointed rather than per-cycle artifacts are approved, the format must losslessly prove every cycle and expose gaps, restart boundaries, and the first anomaly.

Monotonic ledger for cycles 1-10000 with durable reset, LTSSM, enumeration, link, and result data
Correlated AER, dmesg/journal, GPU, BMC/SEL, console, thermal, power, and tool-health evidence
First-fault/abort/recovery or clean post-soak state and engineer verdict

review_improvement: Preserves the extreme reset-soak coverage while adding transaction-level traceability and a hard first-fault boundary so a reset storm cannot mask or amplify failures.
independent_technical_reasoning: A PCIe reset loop is sequentially stateful: cycle N+1 is meaningful only if cycle N completed, the intended endpoint re-enumerated, and the link and error state were accepted. If the tool continues after endpoint loss or a logging failure, later reset counts can be numerically complete but technically invalid. Durable evidence must therefore commit the outcome before releasing the next reset. Because SBR scope follows bridge topology, an incorrect target can reset sibling devices or the host; mapping and out-of-band recovery are safety prerequisites, not optional log enrichment.
